Generate random parameters of a generalized Lotka-Volterra model from an adjacency matrix

Source: R/RcppExports.R
generateGLVparmsFromAdj.Rd

Builds the parameters needed by metaWebNetAssemblyGLV() (interaction matrix, intrinsic growth rates and migration rates) from a matrix that only defines the structure of the interactions, for example one generated with generateRandomGLVadjMat(). The input matrix is not modified.

Usage

generateGLVparmsFromAdj(
  adjM,
  ef,
  predIntAvg = 0.01,
  selfLimAvg = as.numeric(c(0.01, 0.01, 0.01)),
  migrAvg = 0,
  preserveInt = 0L,
  predIntSd = 0.01,
  rndType = 0L
)

Arguments

adjM

Numeric square matrix with the structure of the interactions. Only the signs and the zeros are used when preserveInt = 0; with preserveInt 1 or 2 the values of the non-zero off-diagonal entries are used as well.

ef

Efficiency of predator-prey interactions: effect on the predator / effect on the prey.

predIntAvg

Average strength of the interactions (predator-prey, competition and mutualism) when preserveInt = 0.

selfLimAvg

Numeric vector of length 3 with the average self-limitation of 1 = mutualistic, 2 = basal and 3 = consumer species (diagonal entries of the interaction matrix).

migrAvg

Average migration rate, the migration of each species is uniform in [0, 2 * migrAvg].

preserveInt

How to define the strength of the interactions:

  • 0: random values defined by rndType with mean predIntAvg.

  • 1: the values of adjM are preserved (off-diagonal entries only).

  • 2: random uniform values with mean given by the value in adjM for each interaction, that is, uniform in [0, 2 * abs(adjM[i, j])].

predIntSd

Standard deviation of the strengths when preserveInt = 0 and rndType = 1 (gamma distribution). For the uniform distribution the sd is fixed at predIntAvg * 2 / sqrt(12).

rndType

Distribution of the strengths when preserveInt = 0: 0 = uniform, 1 = gamma. Other values of preserveInt always use the uniform distribution.

Value

A list with the interaction matrix interM (with the self-limitation in the diagonal), the intrinsic growth rates r and the migration rates m. They can be passed to metaWebNetAssemblyGLV() as metaW, r and m.

Details

The type of each interaction is read from the signs of adjM (adjM[i, j] is the effect of species j on species i):

  • adjM[i, j] < 0 and adjM[j, i] > 0: predator-prey, j is the predator and i the prey. The strength of the effect on the prey is random and the effect on the predator is ef times the effect on the prey, with opposite sign.

  • both negative: competition; both positive: mutualism. Each direction gets its own random strength.

  • adjM[i, j] > 0 and adjM[j, i] == 0: commensalism (i benefits); adjM[i, j] < 0 and adjM[j, i] == 0: amensalism (i is harmed).

The strengths of the interactions (off-diagonal values) are drawn according to preserveInt and rndType.

The remaining parameters depend on the type of each species, which is also deduced from adjM: mutualistic if it takes part in any mutualistic interaction, otherwise basal if it has no resources (it is never the predator in a predator-prey interaction, nor the species j in a commensalism), otherwise consumer. For each type:

  • Self-limitation (diagonal of the interaction matrix): -runif(0, 2 * selfLimAvg[k]), where k is 1 for mutualistic, 2 for basal and 3 for consumer species. The diagonal of adjM is ignored.

  • Intrinsic growth rate r: positive, runif(0, 1), for basal species; negative, -runif(0, 1), for consumers (they need resources to persist); and of random sign, with the same magnitude, for mutualistic species (random obligate mutualism).

  • Migration m: runif(0, 2 * migrAvg) for all species.

There is an equivalent implementation in R, generateGLVparmsFromAdjR(), that gives the same results for the same random seed.

See also

generateRandomGLVadjMat() to generate adjM, generateGLVparmsFromAdjR() for the R implementation, and metaWebNetAssemblyGLV().

Examples

set.seed(1)
adj <- generateRandomGLVadjMat(20, 0.2, c(0.1, 0.3, 0.3, 0.15, 0.15))
parms <- generateGLVparmsFromAdj(adj, ef = 0.1, predIntAvg = 0.01, migrAvg = 0.01)
str(parms)
#> List of 3
#>  $ interM: num [1:20, 1:20] -0.01213 0 0 0 -0.00846 ...
#>  $ r     : num [1:20] 0.0294 -0.0432 -0.1737 -0.9557 -0.1971 ...
#>  $ m     : num [1:20] 0.00673 0.00741 0.01244 0.01307 0.00231 ...

# Gamma distributed interaction strengths
parms <- generateGLVparmsFromAdj(adj, ef = 0.1, predIntAvg = 0.01, predIntSd = 0.001, rndType = 1)
